name: Military Green
lede: Military Green is a dull, yellowish olive from a 2010 crowd color survey, close enough to uniform drab that the name reads as obvious even though no army ever registered it.

sections.title: A descriptive compound
sections.body:
The library's only source for Military Green is the xkcd 2010 survey, where volunteers typed free-text names for colors shown on screen [1]. No dictionary, paint brand or military specification in our data uses the phrase, so its coining is undocumented beyond that survey [1]. It measures lightness 49 and chroma 36 in LCH, a middling, muted olive rather than a pure green [1].

On screen it is close kin to several other olive names: [[velvet-green|Velvet Green]] sits 3.4 CIEDE2000 units away, [[muddy-green|Muddy Green]] 3.6, and [[dirty-green|Dirty Green]] 3.7, all read by the graph as almost the same color; [[khaki-green|Khaki Green]] is a little further off at 4.9, more vivid [2]. The nearest gem comparison is [[gem:peridot|peridot]], whose common stones run a touch deeper [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this olive in 206 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.87%, as photographed; a stricter within-painting reading finds it in 106 [4]. It first turns up in a 1390 painting by Spinello Aretino, 620 years before the name's own 2010 record, which only means an aged photograph can resemble this hue, not that anyone mixed this pigment then [4]. Georges Seurat is its most devoted painter here, present in 8 of his 41 works, 10.4 times the baseline rate [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, the smallest, brightest note rather than the shadow [4].
